text: New jack swing, the late-'80s blend of R&B and hip hop drums, is most closely tied to producer Teddy Riley.
The Roland TR-808 drum machine came out in 1980. Its booming kick became a foundation of hip hop and R&B.
"Rapper's Delight" by the Sugarhill Gang (1979) was the first rap single to reach the Billboard Hot 100's Top 40.
The first Grammy for Best Rap Performance (1989) went to DJ Jazzy Jeff & the Fresh Prince for "Parents Just Don't Understand".
source: Wikipedia: Grammy Award for Best Rap Performance

text: "I'm Coming Out" (1980) was written and produced by Nile Rodgers and Bernard Edwards of Chic.
The Notorious B.I.G. was the first artist with two posthumous No. 1 singles: "Hypnotize" and "Mo Money Mo Problems".
"Mo Money Mo Problems" (1997) is built on a sample of Diana Ross's "I'm Coming Out".
titles: Mo Money Mo Problems (ft. Mase and Puff Daddy)

text: Mase's debut album was "Harlem World" (1997). In 1999 he stepped away from music to pursue ministry.
"Break Your Heart Right Back" (2014) flips the same Diana Ross "I'm Coming Out" sample Biggie used on "Mo Money Mo Problems".
Before Childish Gambino, Donald Glover was a writer on NBC's "30 Rock".
Majid Jordan is the Toronto duo of Majid Al Maskati and Jordan Ullman, signed to Drake's OVO Sound.
Majid Jordan are featured on Drake's "Hold On, We're Going Home" (2013).
source: Wikipedia: Hold On, We're Going Home

text: 112 took their name from Club 112, a nightclub in Atlanta.
112 sing on Puff Daddy and Faith Evans's "I'll Be Missing You" (1997), the tribute to The Notorious B.I.G.
112's "Only You" remix features The Notorious B.I.G. and Mase.
Joe (Joseph Lewis Thomas) was born in Columbus, Georgia, and grew up in Opelika, Alabama.
Joe's "I Wanna Know" (2000) spent months on the Billboard Hot 100 and became one of his biggest hits.
Joe sings the hook on Big Pun's "Still Not a Player" (1998).
Janet Jackson's "Rhythm Nation 1814" (1989) produced seven top-five Billboard Hot 100 singles.
Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis produced Janet Jackson's breakthrough album "Control" (1986).
Robin Thicke is the son of actor Alan Thicke of "Growing Pains".
Robin Thicke's "Lost Without U" (2006) topped the Billboard R&B/Hip-Hop chart.
Donell Jones is from Chicago. His "U Know What's Up" (1999) features Lisa "Left Eye" Lopes of TLC.
Chris Brown's debut single "Run It!" (2005) hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 when he was 16.
Mariah Carey's "Fantasy" (1995) samples Tom Tom Club's "Genius of Love". Its remix features Ol' Dirty Bastard.
The-Dream co-wrote Rihanna's "Umbrella" and Beyoncé's "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)".
New Edition formed in Boston's Roxbury neighborhood. Members went on to Bobby Brown's solo career and Bell Biv DeVoe.
Bell Biv DeVoe (three members of New Edition) broke out with "Poison" in 1990.
Toni Braxton's "Un-Break My Heart" (1996) was written by Diane Warren.
Christina Milian co-wrote Jennifer Lopez's "Play" (2001).
J. Holiday's "Bed" (2007) was written by The-Dream and Tricky Stewart.
Avant is from Cleveland, Ohio. His debut single "Separated" came out in 2000.
Barry White's "Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe" (1974) reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
source: Wikipedia: Can't Get Enough of Your Love, Babe

text: JoJo was 13 when "Leave (Get Out)" (2004) made her the youngest solo artist with a No. 1 on Billboard's pop radio chart.
Cassie's "Me & U" (2006) was written and produced by Ryan Leslie.
Mýa won a Grammy for "Lady Marmalade" (2001) with Christina Aguilera, Lil' Kim and Pink.
Aaliyah's "Are You That Somebody?" (1998) was produced by Timbaland for the "Dr. Dolittle" soundtrack.
Michael Jackson's "Thriller" (1982) is widely cited as the best-selling album of all time.
Fabolous is from Brooklyn. DJ Clue discovered him and signed him to Desert Storm.
Brian McKnight's "Back at One" (1999) is his biggest hit.
Tyrese first got noticed singing on a bus in a 1994 Coca-Cola commercial.
Johnny Gill joined New Edition in 1987, after Bobby Brown left the group.
Sisqó was the lead singer of Dru Hill before "Thong Song" (2000).
Dru Hill named themselves after Druid Hill Park in their hometown, Baltimore.
Total, Bad Boy's girl group, broke out with "Can't You See" featuring The Notorious B.I.G. (1995).
Jagged Edge were signed by Jermaine Dupri to So So Def.
Mario's "Let Me Love You" (2004) was co-written by Ne-Yo and produced by Scott Storch.
source: Wikipedia: Let Me Love You (Mario song)

text: Snoop Dogg's "Doggystyle" (1993), produced by Dr. Dre, debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
Usher's "Yeah!" (2004) features Lil Jon and Ludacris.
2Pac's "Dear Mama" was added to the Library of Congress National Recording Registry in 2010.
Patrice Rushen's "Forget Me Nots" (1982) was interpolated in Will Smith's "Men in Black" (1997).
Fat Joe and Terror Squad's "Lean Back" (2004) reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
Ralph Tresvant's "Sensitivity" (1990) was produced by Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis.
Color Me Badd's "I Wanna Sex You Up" (1991) was on the "New Jack City" soundtrack.
source: Wikipedia: I Wanna Sex You Up

text: Ashanti sings on Ja Rule's "Always on Time" (2001).
Blaque were discovered by Lisa "Left Eye" Lopes of TLC.
Big Sean got signed to Kanye West's GOOD Music after rapping for him at a Detroit radio station.
Xscape, from Atlanta, were discovered by Jermaine Dupri.
Yvonne Fair's "It Should Have Been Me" (1975) was a Motown hit.
LL Cool J's "Around the Way Girl" (1990) samples the Mary Jane Girls' "All Night Long".
Bobby Brown's "My Prerogative" (1988) was produced by Teddy Riley.
Evelyn "Champagne" King recorded "Shame" (1977) as a teenager.
Lloyd's "You" (2007) features Lil Wayne.
"They Can't Take That Away from Me" is a George and Ira Gershwin song, introduced by Fred Astaire in the 1937 film Shall We Dance.
titles: They Can't Take That Away From Me
source: Wikipedia: They Can't Take That Away from Me

text: Diana Krall is a jazz pianist and singer from Nanaimo, British Columbia.
"If You Don't Know Me by Now" was written by Gamble and Huff and first a hit for Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes in 1972. Simply Red's 1989 version went to No. 1 in the US.
titles: If You Don't Know Me By Now
source: Wikipedia: If You Don't Know Me by Now

text: "Holding Back the Years" was Simply Red's first US No. 1, in 1986.
The saxophone solo on Shanice's "I Love Your Smile" (1991) is by Branford Marsalis.
SWV stands for Sisters With Voices.
SWV's "Weak" (1993) went to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
"Set Adrift on Memory Bliss" (1991) is built on Spandau Ballet's "True" and went to No. 1 in the US.
source: Wikipedia: Set Adrift on Memory Bliss

text: P.M. Dawn were brothers Attrell and Jarrett Cordes from Jersey City, New Jersey.
George Michael co-wrote "Careless Whisper" with Andrew Ridgeley as a teenager, years before it became a 1984 hit.
George Michael's Faith won the Grammy for Album of the Year in 1989. "Father Figure" was one of its US No. 1 singles.
Maxwell's "This Woman's Work" is a Kate Bush cover, first performed on his MTV Unplugged in 1997.
Maxwell's debut album was Maxwell's Urban Hang Suite (1996).
Before going solo, Omarion was the lead singer of B2K.
Jodeci are two pairs of brothers from Charlotte, North Carolina: K-Ci and JoJo Hailey, and DeVante Swing and Mr. Dalvin DeGrate.
Timbaland and Missy Elliott got early starts in DeVante Swing's Swing Mob collective, working on Jodeci records.
Jodeci's debut album Forever My Lady (1991) came out on Uptown Records.
Keith Sweat's debut Make It Last Forever (1987) was co-produced with Teddy Riley, a cornerstone of new jack swing.
The title track "Make It Last Forever" is a duet with Jacci McGhee.
Tevin Campbell was discovered by Quincy Jones and sang lead on "Tomorrow (A Better You, Better Me)" from Back on the Block (1989).
"Can We Talk" (1993) was written and produced by Babyface.
source: Wikipedia: Can We Talk (Tevin Campbell song)

text: Mint Condition are from St. Paul, Minnesota. "Breakin' My Heart (Pretty Brown Eyes)" came out on Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis's Perspective Records.
Babyface is Kenneth Edmonds. Bootsy Collins gave him the nickname.
Babyface wrote "I'll Make Love to You" for Boyz II Men. It held No. 1 for 14 weeks in 1994.
source: Wikipedia: I'll Make Love to You

text: "End of the Road" (1992), from the Boomerang soundtrack, held No. 1 for 13 weeks.
source: Wikipedia: End of the Road (Boyz II Men song)

text: Boyz II Men formed at the Philadelphia High School for Creative and Performing Arts.
D'Angelo's debut Brown Sugar (1995) is a landmark of neo soul.
"Cruisin'" on Brown Sugar is a Smokey Robinson cover.
"Devil's Pie" was produced by DJ Premier and appears on D'Angelo's Voodoo (2000).
Before his own hits, Ne-Yo co-wrote Mario's "Let Me Love You" (2004).
Tony! Toni! Toné! came from Oakland: brothers Raphael Saadiq and D'wayne Wiggins with their cousin Timothy Christian Riley.
Lionel Richie sang "All Night Long (All Night)" at the closing ceremony of the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.
"The Ghetto" (1970), from Everything Is Everything, was co-written by Donny Hathaway and Leroy Hutson.
Sade is both the band and its singer, Sade Adu, born in Ibadan, Nigeria. It's pronounced "shah-day".
Sade's debut album Diamond Life (1984) included "Your Love Is King" and "Smooth Operator".
Ginuwine's debut single "Pony" (1996) was produced by Timbaland.
Anita Baker's "Sweet Love", from Rapture (1986), won the Grammy for Best R&B Song.
Before going solo, Anita Baker sang with the Detroit band Chapter 8.
"Night Fever" and "How Deep Is Your Love" both come from the Saturday Night Fever soundtrack, and both went to No. 1.
"I Wanna Be Your Lover" (1979) was Prince's first big hit, a No. 1 R&B single.
source: Wikipedia: I Wanna Be Your Lover

text: "The Most Beautiful Girl in the World" (1994) came out while Prince went by an unpronounceable symbol.
titles: The Most Beautiful Girl In The World
source: Wikipedia: The Most Beautiful Girl in the World (Prince song)

text: The Commodores formed at Tuskegee Institute in Alabama. Lionel Richie wrote "Easy" (1977).
Gino Vannelli is from Montreal. "I Just Wanna Stop" (1978) was his biggest US hit.
Ashanti, from Glen Cove, New York, broke out on Irv Gotti's Murder Inc. label. She also sings on Lloyd's "Southside" (2004).
"I Want You" (1976) was written by Leon Ware and Arthur "T-Boy" Ross.
source: Wikipedia: I Want You (Marvin Gaye song)

text: Sinéad Harnett is an R&B singer-songwriter from London.
Yvonne Elliman played Mary Magdalene in Jesus Christ Superstar, on the 1970 album and in the 1973 film.
"If I Can't Have You" was written by the Bee Gees for Saturday Night Fever and went to No. 1 for Yvonne Elliman in 1978.
source: Wikipedia: If I Can't Have You (Bee Gees song)

text: "Hello Stranger" was first a 1963 hit for Barbara Lewis.
Ready for the World came from Flint, Michigan. "Oh Sheila" went to No. 1 in 1985.
"Like a Prayer" (1989) went to No. 1 in the US and the UK.
Jesse Powell is from Gary, Indiana. "You" was his biggest hit, reaching the US top 10.
"Let Me Love You" (2016) is from DJ Snake's debut album Encore.
source: Wikipedia: Let Me Love You (DJ Snake song)

text: Isaac Hayes was the first African American to win the Oscar for Best Original Song, for "Theme from Shaft".
"Never Gonna Give You Up" was first recorded by Jerry Butler. Hayes's long version is on Black Moses (1971).
Herb Alpert's "Rise" (1979) went to No. 1, and The Notorious B.I.G. built "Hypnotize" (1997) on it.
"Sorry" (2015), from Purpose, went to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
"Eternal Flame" (1989) went to No. 1 in both the US and the UK.
Baby, later known as Birdman, co-founded Cash Money Records with his brother Ronald "Slim" Williams.
"Jealous" (2014) was Nick Jonas's first big solo hit after the Jonas Brothers.
"Baby Baby" (1991), from Heart in Motion, went to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100.
"September" (1978) was written by Maurice White, Al McKay and Allee Willis.
George Benson's Give Me the Night (1980) was produced by Quincy Jones.
"Into the Night" (1980) charted twice in the US: first in 1980, then again in 1989.
source: Wikipedia: Into the Night (Benny Mardones song)

text: "Summer Madness" (1974) was used in the film Rocky (1976).
Simply Red formed in Manchester, England, in 1985, fronted by Mick Hucknall.
